title: Whole Woody Axis and Open Paired Follicles Banksia
description: One wholly newly authored complete mature Banksia-like woody infructescence, about fifteen centimetres tall with its short cut stalk. An elongated irregular woody rachis bears twelve separate transversely oriented follicles in staggered tiers; each follicle retains both complete thick concave woody valves, opened oppositely at their embedded rear roots to expose a real mouth and inner faces. The axis, valve bowls, hinge relationships and all numeric coordinates are new, not conifer scales or artichoke bracts arranged on a different stem, nor a rearranged star-anise fruit. Banksia is an angiosperm and this fruiting head is not a true conifer cone. One complete detached fruiting head model, zero scenes and no separately counted valves; not a whole shrub or flowering spike. Four quiet opaque woody PBR roles and actual low relief, no texture cards. Generic weathered post-release exterior art; exact species, follicle count biology, persistent flower detail, retained seeds or separators, internal tissue and heat-triggered opening are not reconstructed. No fire, germination, seed-release mechanism, ecology, preparation, food, treatment or physical stability claim. Finite cut-stalk datum is only static presentation. No labels, rig, animation or interaction.
